What this page binds: the {strategy} at claim-set version {editionVersion}, the current prior-art comparison matrix, and its passage map. Matrix scores are issue-spotting aids, not conclusions, and this page is not an admission.
The two panes: the claims pane lists every claim limitation with its matrix obligations; the disclosure pane shows prior-art obligation cards, candidate passages, and full transcriptions.

Obligation states: every matrix obligation keeps its authored exact state. Counsel review required records a material relationship with no exact candidate passage; neutral review allocations identify fragments for counsel review.
Emphasis: only the passages of the selected candidate receive forward emphasis, the opposite convention from the specification navigator. Passages of every other candidate stay unmarked.
The scoring legend: P marks a concrete partial or analogous mapping; an em dash marks no concrete whole-claim mapping. Neither score is an obviousness conclusion or a clearance.

Movement: activate a limitation to reach its candidate passages and matrix obligations. In the forward bar, {candidatePrevious} and {candidateNext} wrap candidate movement and reset the passage index; {passagePrevious} and {passageNext} wrap passage movement within the selected candidate. Reverse badges return to the related claims, where {movePrevious} and {moveNext} wrap reverse movement. {clear} clears the selection from either bar. The reader button opens the full transcription at the exact passage.

Review posture and version binding: a comparison matrix is valid only for the claim-set version named in its header. This page is a draft counsel-review aid and an ephemeral technical preview, not a legal opinion of any kind, and not an admission; it presents one claim strategy. PDF source evidence remains the fidelity authority, and transcription uncertainty remains visible. Anchor references are internal navigation labels, not official numbering, and must not be cited. Human review of the source PDF evidence remains authoritative.
